title: Scheduled Run Receipts
user: A small-team operator with cron jobs, queues, or scheduled workflows who needs to prove both that a run occurred and that a missed expected run was noticed.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN asks how teams monitor cron jobs and queue workers because URL uptime cannot show whether a scheduler stopped or a worker crashed.
The author describes the key absence-detection problem: a missed scheduled run leaves no log line to inspect.

recurrence: Two 2026 sources independently focus on missed work rather than ordinary endpoint uptime; this is a high-severity silent-failure class for small operations.
current_workaround: Ping an uptime service from scripts, watch logs manually, or discover the gap through stale downstream data.
incumbents_and_gap: Healthchecks.io, Better Uptime, Uptime Kuma, and framework-specific monitors accept pings, but do not make an expected-run calendar plus portable, per-run evidence the primary local artifact.
smallest_useful_product: A CLI plus static viewer that reads an expected schedule, accepts signed run-start/run-finish receipts, detects missing/late/overlapping runs, and exports a weekly HTML evidence page.
constraints: Receipt endpoints need replay protection and short retention; all schedule and run metadata should remain local by default.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, the tool detects 100% of deliberately skipped runs within the configured grace window and operators can identify the last known successful run in under two minutes.
why_distinct: It is an absence detector and evidence trail, not another dashboard that merely displays received pings.
